newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB on course for 1998 digital TV launch.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB on course for 1998 digital TV launch.

text.p: Pay television operator British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc said on Friday it was on course to launch its digital satellite service in the UK in the spring of next year.

The company, which will go into the digital era under new management as chief executive Sam Chisholm steps down, said trading in the first six weeks of its 1997/98 financial year was in line with the period a year ago.
BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp has a 40 percent stake, announced pre-tax profits of 314 million pounds ($499.3 million) in the year to June 30 1997.
It received a 14 million pound advance contribution on a programme supply deal for the British Digital Broadcasting venture formed by UK TV companies Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group.
The company said its revenue base should grow this year but added that programming and marketing costs would rise.

"The growth in the number of subscribers, together with the higher level of subscription charges, will increase the company's revenue base. Against this, the company has increased commitments to programming and marketing costs as it prepares for the launch of its digital services," BSkyB said.

BSkyB said its digital service, expected to carry some 200 channels, would feature an extended range of basic and premium channels and a near video-on-demand movie service. It said it was negotiating with Hollywood studios for film pay-per-view rights.
Interactive services such as home shopping and banking will be added to the digital offering later next year.
BSkyB said there were now 5.9 million Sky subscribers in the UK -- 25 percent of all homes -- and a further half a million in Ireland. ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
